description: The enterprise policy model. Everything an organization, a project, or a single repository is ALLOWED to do — autonomy, permissions, data handling, quality gates, cost — expressed as data so a customer-specific policy never requires a change to the platform.

_resolution.rule: Most specific wins, key by key. A repository may only NARROW what its project allows, never widen it. Widening is refused at load time and reported, rather than silently honoured — a policy engine that can be relaxed from inside the thing it governs is not a policy engine.

_levels.0: Explain only. The agent describes and proposes; it writes nothing.
_levels.1: Suggest code. Diffs are shown, never applied.
_levels.2: Write code. Every edit requires developer approval before it lands.
_levels.3: Write, test and self-correct within a repository. No branch, no PR, no deploy.
_levels.4: Open a pull request automatically. Human review still gates the merge.

autonomy.grantRequiredAbove: An organization admin sets `autonomy.level` above 3 in an organization or project block, and the grant is recorded in the decision log. A repository cannot raise its own level.
autonomy.rationale: Levels 0-3 are where an agent is useful and its mistakes stay inside a working tree. Level 4 puts an artifact in front of colleagues, and level 5 changes something customers touch. The jump in blast radius between 3 and 4 is much larger than between any other adjacent pair, which is why the default ceiling sits exactly there.
enforcedBy: hooks/runtime/handlers/autonomy-gate.js — denies the tool call that would exceed the level
scripts/pipeline.py — refuses to advance into a phase the level does not permit

permissions._note: The AI permission model. Per agent, because 'the orchestrator may deploy' and 'the reviewer may deploy' are very different claims. Deny always beats allow; an empty allow list means the agent may only read.

capabilityDefinitions.repo.read: Read source, history and configuration in the active repository.
capabilityDefinitions.repo.write: Modify source files in the active repository.
capabilityDefinitions.repo.write.tests: Modify files matching the stack's test pattern only.
capabilityDefinitions.scan.run: Execute static analysis, dependency and secret scanners.
capabilityDefinitions.graph.build: Build or refresh the structural index.
capabilityDefinitions.tracker.write: Create or comment on issues in a configured tracker.

dataPolicy._note: What may enter a prompt, what may leave the machine, and how long anything is kept. These are the questions a customer security review asks first, and 'we scan for secrets' is only one of them.
dataPolicy.sourceCodeEgressNote: True because the model runs as a hosted service. State this plainly to a customer rather than implying local inference. An air-gapped deployment needs a local model and is out of scope for v3.1 — see docs/CLAUDE-DEPLOYMENT-AND-DESIGN.md.
dataPolicy.retentionNote: Zero means this system stores neither prompts nor responses. Transcripts belong to the harness and follow its own retention. The only things this system persists are: the local telemetry ledger (counts and durations, never content), the egress ledger (hashes and byte counts, never payloads), memory entries (redaction-scanned before write), and the decision log.

qualityGate._note: The gate is a CONJUNCTION, not a score. An AI review is one input among several, and it is never the deciding one — a model grading work produced by the same family of model is not an independent check, and treating it as one is how a quality bar quietly becomes a formality.

coverage.appliesWhen: the repository already has a coverage tool configured

aiAssessment.note: Blocks below the threshold, but passing it is never sufficient on its own.

qualityGate.rule: advance IF every deterministic check passes AND aiAssessment >= minimumScore AND humanReview is satisfied for the current autonomy level. A deterministic check that could not RUN counts as a failure, never as a pass.

approvalPolicy._note: Four named gates. Each names a decision a human owns and an artifact they review, because 'approve?' with nothing attached trains people to click yes.

gates.artifact: the restated requirement and its acceptance criteria
gates.question: Is this what was actually asked for?

gates.artifact: the impact map: every file and layer that changes, each cited
gates.question: Is this the right change to make?

gates.artifact: the diff, the review score and the verification output
gates.question: Would you merge this?

gates.artifact: the readiness verdict, the migration list and the rollback note
gates.question: Are you willing to be paged for this?

approvalPolicy.enforcedBy: hooks/runtime/handlers/human-gate.js blocks the Stop event while a gate artifact has no verdict file. The agent cannot clear its own gate.
approvalPolicy.timeoutNote: Deliberately no auto-approve on timeout. A gate that approves itself after an interval is not a gate, and the failure it permits arrives at 3am on a Friday.

memoryPolicy._note: Memory that syncs organization-wide is a broadcast channel. A wrong entry is not a local mistake; it is re-injected as context into every future session in every repository, and nothing downstream re-derives it.
memoryPolicy.autoPromoteNote: False, deliberately. Confidence and repo-count are necessary and not sufficient: they measure how often something was observed, not whether it is true. A human names the entry as organizational guidance before it becomes organizational guidance.

costLimits._note: Off by default because a limit nobody set is a limit nobody agreed to. Turn it on per organization or project with real numbers.

telemetry.note: Local JSONL, hash-chained, counts and durations only — never prompt or response content. Default-off because telemetry somebody did not switch on is telemetry they did not consent to. Switch it on to produce a real number instead of an asserted one.

model._note: Read by the headless path only. The interactive path uses whatever model the user's Claude Code session is running, and this system deliberately does not override it — silently swapping a person's model mid-session is a surprising thing to do.
model.routingRationale: Verification and indexing are high-volume and mechanical; judgement work is low-volume and expensive to get wrong. Routing the cheap tier at the mechanical skills is the single largest cost lever in the system.
model.fallbackNote: No silent cross-family fallback. If the chosen model is unavailable the run FAILS and says so — a result produced by a different model than the one recorded is an unattributable result, and the eval scores stop meaning anything.
